newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares down at noon on clampdown fears.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares down at noon on clampdown fears.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were down sharply at midday on Tuesday on rumours that the securities authorities were planning more measures to cool down the markets, brokers said.
The B index fell 2.383 points or 2.49 percent to 93.411 points on volume of 11.947 million worth $9.108 million, compared with $9.59 million on Monday.
Institutions are seen offsetting their positions today, increasing investor fears that more solid measures to rein in the markets will be announced in the short term, brokers said.
"Institutions have begun to sell shares, which means there new measures are to be introduced to cool down the overheating stock markets," one broker said.
"This triggered follow-up selling, pulling the index down further," he said.
"With the market having risen so sharply over the past few weeks, the correction range will be 10-20 percent," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 38 traded, with 30 down, four flat and four up.
Shanghai Vacuum & Electron Device was the biggest loser on profit-taking, plunging $0.020 or 8.19 percent to $0.224 on volume of 186,900 shares.
Shanghai Chlor Alkali Chemical was the most actively traded on institutional unwind selling, slipping $0.008 or 2.18 percent to $0.358 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index was down on heavy profit-taking on the same concerns, brokers said.
The index dipped 21.875 points or 1.39 percent to 1,547.124 points on volume of 506.5 million shares worth 6.8 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 42.087 points or 0.98 percent to 4,244.095 points.
Shanghai No.1 Department Store was the biggest loser on major institutional liquidation selling, plunging 1.40 yuan or 8.13 percent to 15.80 yuan on volume of 4.8 million shares.
